name: Florida
status_why: The Division's flat file answered scripts.
system: Two state systems: Florida Election Watch (floridaelectionwatch.gov, the Division of Elections' election-night site, with flat-file downloads) and the older Election Results Reporting System (results.elections.myflorida.com). Counties run their own ENR, most on VR Systems' enr.electionsfl.org.

election.how_to_find: The file name follows the date; it appears on the night.

feeds.address: https://flelectionfiles.floridados.gov/enightfilespublic/<yyyymmdd>_ElecResultsFL.txt (tab-delimited: ElectionDate, PartyCode, PartyName, RaceCode, RaceName, CountyCode, CountyName, Juris1num, Juris2num, Precincts, PrecinctsReporting, CanNameLast, CanNameFirst, CanNameMiddle, CanVotes); pipe-delimited pair <yyyymmdd>_ElecResultsFL_PipeDlm_Info.txt and _PipeDlm_Votes.txt; an Excel file too (Downloads page)
feeds.updates: Election night from 8:00 p.m. Eastern (the site says results are not released before then because of two time zones); refreshed as counties upload.
feeds.note: 20241105_ElecResultsFL.txt answered 200 to a script on 2026-10-09 (392,733 bytes, application/octet-stream). The Downloads page lists 20260818 files for the Aug 18 primary.

feeds.address: Same file (RaceCode USS, USR; county rows)
Same file (State Senate, State Representative, multi-county and circuit judicial offices)

feeds.note: The older Data Extract Utility answered 200 for ElectionDate=11/5/2024; fl.py reads it (OfficialResults=Y).

feeds.address: https://enr.electionsfl.org/<3-letter county code>/<election id>/Summary/ (VR Systems county ENR; also /Precincts/ and /Map/PrecinctsReporting)
feeds.note: enr.electionsfl.org/LEV/3693/Summary/ (Levy, 2024 general) answered 200 (167 KB HTML, Amazon S3). Each county's election id differs; data files behind the pages not checked.

races_in_feed: State files: federal, statewide, legislature, multi-county offices and circuit judges, county by county. County ENR sites: county commission, school board, constitutional officers, cities, special districts.
local: Yes, all 67. Most use VR Systems ENR at enr.electionsfl.org/<CODE>/ (LEV, DIX seen); the biggest (Miami-Dade, Broward, Palm Beach, Hillsborough, Orange) run their own supervisor sites, addresses not checked today.
how_counted: Florida counts mail and early ballots before polls close and releases them first, from 8 p.m. Eastern.
count_order: Mail and early votes first; county ENR sites split Election Day, Early Voting and Vote-by-Mail.
vote_types: Not in the state file (county totals only). Many county ENR sites show Election Day, Early Voting and Vote-by-Mail columns; Florida counts mail ballots before polls close and releases them first, so the count-order predictor has a strong known pattern. Check per county.

certify.rule: Meets at 8 a.m. on the 14th day after the election (Fla. Stat. 102.111).
certify.local_rule: Counties file returns by noon on the 13th day (Fla. Stat. 102.112).
certify.source: NCSL, 'Election Certification Deadlines' (www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/certification-deadlines), read 2026-10-10; secondary: a summary of each state's law, not the law itself

terms: None stated on the Downloads page.
scout_blocked: Nothing refused scripts. The candidate download (dos.elections.myflorida.com) also answers scripts.
scout_plan: Live-readable. On election night fetch 20261103_ElecResultsFL.txt every 3 to 5 minutes from 8:00 p.m. Eastern; it gives every federal, statewide and legislative race by county with precincts reporting. Local races: start with the counties on enr.electionsfl.org (find each county's election id the week before) and add the large self-hosted supervisors one at a time. Use the counties' vote-type columns for the count-order model, since Florida's mail and early votes come first.
notes: The file gives county rows only; a contest's whole figure is the sum of its counties. The address answers 404 until the night's file is posted.
certified(): the Division's Summary Report (results.elections.myflorida.com SummaryRpt.asp, Race=FED) once it says Official Results.
sources: NCSL, 'Election Certification Deadlines' (www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/certification-deadlines), read 2026-10-10; secondary: a summary of each state's law, not the law itself
